text:
alex: FYI — ACME hitting lots of 401s after they upgraded python-sdk to 0.9.2 yesterday. They also reported a couple of duplicate billing entries (same call charged twice) — looks like retries are firing. Attaching trimmed logs below.

alex: ```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Mon, 18 Nov 2024 17:12:45 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "message": "missing api key"
}
Trace: client.request() -> raised 401 at request.go:123
```

sam: Thanks — can you paste the SDK versions for python/ts/go they have in their deps? Also which endpoint (region) were they hitting?

alex: Python 0.9.2, JS 0.8.6 (they didn't upgrade JS), Go 0.6.1. Region: us-east-1 (prod). Customer says it started ~after they rolled python bump.

maria: Interesting — quick hypothesis: OpenAPI/security change slipped in last spec push. If codegen produced a different header name or auth wrapper for python only, that would explain per-SDK failures.

maria: Can you share the exact request headers from the python client log?

alex: ```
Request: POST /v1/generate
Headers: {
  "authorization": "Bearer REDACTED",
  "content-type": "application/json"
}
```

alex: Note header key is lowercase `authorization`. server logs show it didn't find api key header.

kevin: On runtime side we recently accepted both `Authorization` and `X-Api-Key` for a transition (deployed to canary + eu region), but us-east only has the strict check (Authorization bearer). If python client changed to send `authorization` instead of `Authorization` maybe upstream header normalization failed in a proxy layer?

jen: Hm lowercase header keys shouldn't matter — proxies normalize. But I remember a recent OpenAPI change switching security scheme from `apiKey` (in header `X-Api-Key`) to `http`/bearer. Codegen generators interpret that into different auth helpers. If python generator picked the old `X-Api-Key` wrapper but code actually expects bearer, you get 401.

sam: That maps to the customer's report: they only bumped python. JS still working. So python generated client is now sending a different shape header or wrapper.

maria: I pulled the last spec change: GH #987 changed components.securitySchemes from name `ApiKeyAuth` (type: apiKey, in: header, name: X-Api-Key) to `BearerAuth` (type: http, scheme: bearer). The commit message said "align spec with authv2". Looks like codegen produced new helper functions in python but our python SDK release 0.9.2 included partial regen that changed the auth helper to expect a token in a kw param `api_key` (legacy) but also injected `Authorization` differently. There's a generation mismatch across SDK repos — CI didn't trigger regen for JS/Go because of a brittle path matcher in sdk-gen pipeline.

maria: TL;DR: OpenAPI update + CI regen drift -> inconsistent auth behavior across SDKs. That would also explain retries/billing if the python client does an automatic retry on 401 and the server registers the initial attempt in billing before failing — leading to duplicate charge entries.

kevin: Also saw a pattern where client lib would attempt an auth refresh and re-send the request without idempotency key. That causes observable duplicate side-effects for non-idempotent endpoints.

alex: Customer is on a tight window — they want a patch or guidance.

jen: Short term: add gateway shim to accept both `X-Api-Key` and `Authorization` headers for us-east to stop 401s. I'll open an infra rollback/patch PR. Medium term: force-regenerate all SDKs from canonical spec and bump major where auth wrapper semantics changed.

maria: Action items I can run:
- Add a spec-check job to sdk-gen CI that fails if securitySchemes change without a manual approval.
- Kick off immediate regen for python/js/go and cut hotfix releases with a note in changelog about auth fix.

sam: Please create a support-facing blurb to send to ACME explaining we're rolling a compatibility shim and will cut SDK hotfixes. Also ask them to avoid rolling to 0.9.2 until we confirm.

jen: Created infra PR: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/425 — gateway will accept both headers in us-east and add normalized header for runtime. Will ship after one more review.

maria: I'm opening SDK regen issue: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-regeneration/issues/112 (regen-run, bump versions, changelog entry). I'll attach quick repro for maintainers:
```bash
# repro with python 0.9.2
python -c "from redwood import RedwoodClient; c=RedwoodClient(token=\"x\"); c.generate(\"hi\")"
# server responds 401 on us-east before shim
```

sam: Great; I'll send customer note and mark this P1. cc: @kevin @maria @jen.

acme-rep: Thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll hold the roll to other services until you confirm. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: CI pipeline triggered for sdk-regeneration repo (job 1145) — regen step started.

maria: Will follow up here when hotfix releases are published. Also adding a permanent CI gating rule so this drift doesn't surprise us again.

jen: Patch merged to canary, rolling to us-east under a limited flag. Monitoring for 10m.

kevin: Runtime logs show 401 rate for ACME down to 0. next steps: release python 0.9.3 containing auth fix + patch changelog noting security scheme change.

maria: Filed rst for release notes, linking GH #112 and infra PR #425. Closing loop once packages published.

sam: Thanks all — I'll update the ticket and let ACME know. :pray:
